about.title: Patterson Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Patterson residents rely on a small number of clinics and outlying hospitals for care, and when something goes wrong during treatment, the aftermath can be confusing and isolating. Medical malpractice differs from a car crash claim — California's MICRA law imposes a short window to act, a mandatory 90-day notice before filing suit, and requires a qualified medical expert to establish that a provider fell below the accepted standard of care. Not every bad result qualifies; the law distinguishes between an unfortunate outcome and an actual departure from proper medical practice. If you or a family member were harmed by a delayed diagnosis, medication mix-up, or surgical error in the Patterson area, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these claims and can explain, without cost, whether your situation may fit the legal definition of malpractice. There's no obligation to move forward after that conversation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Time Runs Out

items.title: MICRA's Clock Is Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim — an attorney can help you figure out where you stand.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed, California law requires 90 days' advance notice to the provider, so early legal guidance helps avoid missing procedural steps.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm the standard of care was breached, having an attorney who can arrange that review is often essential to a viable claim.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result alone doesn't mean a provider was negligent. Malpractice requires showing the provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, which is why an expert review is almost always necessary.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in Patterson?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from when it occurred, whichever comes first. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth having a timeline reviewed early rather than assuming you still have time.

items.question: Are there limits on what I can recover?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) in malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap.
